verdict: READY TO MERGE - 12 of 12 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: GOLDEN compares the default capture byte for byte, so merge-mode output can only change by the one added '- Mode: merge' line.
All three mode forms (--squash, -s, bare squash) are run and their captures compared for identical output, and build is checked for each form against the saved TXT and the receipt.
The tests run real behavior: only the gh seam is faked, and real make_project git repos and the real driver main() are used. There are no mock-chain wiring tests.
Rebuilding without a flag is tested both ways (squash and merge subjects), and the squash-subject path still runs the Conventional-Commit title check.
Unknown mode tokens are refused in both capture and build, and the build case also checks that no TXT is written.
The contract-test additions use strings the base did not contain (argument-hint, 'squash message', 'squash mode' in HARNESS_RULES.md), so each one can fail.

fetch_view / check_title split lets run_build decide the mode from line 1 before the title check, so a saved squash TXT rebuilds without the flag and the run_build docstring states that ordering exactly.
Explicit --squash with a merge-form subject is refused before the squash title check (merge_commit_msg.py:387-388), so the actionable 'drop the squash mode' hint is never masked by a title refusal.
squash_mode refuses an unknown positional mode token instead of silently treating it as merge mode, and it runs before config activation so the error is cheap.
Every new parameter defaults to merge mode (squash=False), keeping existing callers and the default capture output unchanged apart from the added '- Mode: merge' fact.
Docstrings were updated in step with each signature change; the linear docstring-vs-code pass found no contradiction in merge_commit_msg.py beyond the squash title rule.

SKILL.md, message_format.md and README.md match the driver on the mode handoff: build with the flag needs the squash subject, without it detects either exact subject, and the merge-subject-under-squash hint (merge_commit_msg.py:331-333) is described as the code prints it.

The squash worked example in message_format.md passes the build rules as written: the title is a Type(scope) title, there are 4 bullets, every line is under 110 columns, no filler or SHA, and the receipt matches receipt() (`squash message for PR #N`).

The SKILL.md argument rule closes the gap between the three user forms and the one command form (`--squash`), and states that a `squash` after `--` is guidance, which matches D6 and the driver's positional and flag parsing.
The fresh strap spec ties each behavior to named pytest nodes; the archived spec keeps the old frozen record intact under `_archive/`, as D2 chose.
Squash title check runs in check_title before any diff or commit fetch, so a non-Conventional title fails fast in capture.
run_build orders the cross-mode subject check before the squash title check, and its docstring states why (the drop-the-flag hint is not masked); code and docstring agree.
subject_parts is reused from harness_lib.commit_txt (private alias kept) instead of a second Conventional-Commit regex in the skill.
Mode is surfaced in capture facts, the output header, the build instruction (`build --squash`) and the receipt, so the agent can carry it from capture to build without remembering it.
Module docstring, SKILL.md, message_format.md, README and HARNESS_RULES.md agree on the three mode forms, both subjects, the shared PR<N>_merge.txt name and flagless rebuild.
The squash worked example obeys the format card's own rules (Conventional title that parses, no SHAs, column-0 layout, lineage after bullets, line widths under 110).
No orphan or renamed references: branch-commit-msg Step 5, guard_commit_txt.py and the SkillSpec all still point at the same skill name and TXT name.

Splitting fetch_view from check_title lets build pick the mode from line 1 before the title check runs. A merge subject under --squash gets the 'drop the squash mode' hint instead of being hidden behind a squash-only title refusal, as the run_build docstring explains.

D4 flag-or-detect keeps the existing change route intact: the guard hook's 'build <N>' and the HARNESS_RULES rebuild rule work for a saved squash TXT without a flag, and the merge-mode TXT and receipt are byte-identical to before.

test_merge_commit_msg_squash.py is behavioral throughout. gh is the only stub; capture and build go through main() against a make_project repo and assert stdout, stderr, the exit code and the TXT on disk. GOLDEN pins the full no-mode capture output.
The squash title check reuses commit_txt's one subject parser, made public, instead of a second regex (D1). The private alias keeps the module's internal callers unchanged, and a test pins the alias.

Docs stay consistent across SKILL.md, message_format.md, README and HARNESS_RULES: all name the three mode forms, both subjects, the shared PR<N>_merge.txt name and the 'squash message' receipt, and the contract tests pin each claim.
Unknown mode tokens give a problem: line with exit 1 (D5) rather than argparse's exit 2 usage dump, which matches the skill's problem-line handling.

important.name: Squash title check accepts any word before a colon, not the project's commit types
important.summary:
title_problem's squash branch (merge_commit_msg.py:136-140) validates the PR title with subject_parts, which matches the loose parser regex _SUBJECT (commit_txt.py:40, `^([A-Za-z]+)(?:\(([^)]*)\))?:\s*(.*)$`). That regex was built to locate a subject inside a TXT block, not to validate one: titles such as `WIP: rework capture`, `Re: review notes`, `Feat: squash mode`, `Fixed:x` (no space) or `https://example.com/x` all return a type and a non-empty summary, so capture and build accept them and the squash commit lands on main with a subject outside the type list in reference/commit_format.md. The same module already holds the real rule, _HEADER_RULE (commit_txt.py:47, Feature|Fix|Refactor|Test|Build|Docs|Chore with an optional space-free scope and `: \S`), which branch-commit-msg enforces. The module docstring (merge_commit_msg.py:8), the error text ('Type(scope): summary') and message_format.md:50 promise a Conventional-Commit subject; the check delivers 'any alphabetic word and a colon'.

Also (overall): title_problem() in squash mode needs only subject_parts() to return a type and a non-empty summary. The shared _SUBJECT regex (commit_txt.py:40, ^([A-Za-z]+)(?:\(([^)]*)\))?:\s*(.*)$) matches any run of letters followed by a colon, so titles like 'WIP: draft', 'Re: export crash' or 'Note: see issue' pass. README.md:345, message_format.md (Verbatim title) and the module docstring all say the title 'must be a Conventional-Commit subject (Type(scope): summary)'. D1 chose this parser on purpose, so the regex is not the defect. The docs overstate what the check enforces.
fix: Add a public predicate in commit_txt.py, e.g. `def header_rule_ok(header: str) -> bool: return bool(_HEADER_RULE.match(header))`, and use it in title_problem's squash branch in place of the subject_parts call (subject_parts then needs no export for this driver); add a test that `WIP: x` and `Feat: x` are refused while `Feature(merge-commit-msg): add squash mode` passes.

If the looser rule is intended, say so: change the docstring at merge_commit_msg.py:8, the problem text at merge_commit_msg.py:139 and message_format.md:50 to 'a `Word(scope): summary` subject' so the contract matches the check.
Soften the doc wording to what is enforced ('a `Type(scope): summary` shape: a word, an optional scope, a colon and a summary') in README.md, message_format.md and the module docstring.
Or, through a plan decision, check the type against the project's commit-type list if one is configured.

important.name: Merge-subject-under-squash test cannot catch removal of the early refusal it exists for
important.summary: run_build (merge_commit_msg.py:384-390) refuses a merge-form line 1 under --squash before check_title, and its docstring says this is so the hint to drop the squash mode is not masked by a title the squash mode refuses. test_squash_build_names_the_flag_on_a_merge_subject only uses TITLE, which is a Conventional-Commit title, so check_title passes and subject_problem returns the same hint through message_problems. Delete lines 387-388 and the test still passes, so the ordering guarantee has no test. The assertions are also loose: '--squash' and 'merge' would match many other messages, and nothing checks that the squash subject is printed.
fix: Add a case that runs _build(module, root, monkeypatch, capsys, f"Merge PR #7 -- {LEGACY_TITLE}", "--squash", title=LEGACY_TITLE) and asserts code == 1, _txt(root) is None, 'subject is the merge form' in captured.err and 'Conventional-Commit' not in captured.err.
Tighten the existing assertion to 'subject is the merge form' in captured.err and repr(SQUASH) in captured.err.

minor.summary: All five items in 0008_merge_commit_msg_squash_mode_ActionPlan.json (and the rendered PIP) read status PENDING with evidence 'not started', yet the branch carries the commits that do TASK-1 to TASK-5 (subject_parts, driver squash mode, docs, spec freeze). minor.name: Private alias _subject_parts duplicates the new public name for two in-module callers
minor.summary: commit_txt.py:147 keeps `_subject_parts = subject_parts` only so the two call sites in the same module (lines 162 and 208) need not change; no other file calls the private name (tests/lib/test_commit_txt_subject_parts.py:29 merely pins the alias). Two names for one function inside one module is dead indirection that a later rename has to keep in sync.
fix: Call subject_parts at commit_txt.py:162 and :208, delete the alias at line 147, and drop test_private_name_is_the_same_function from tests/lib/test_commit_txt_subject_parts.py.

minor.name: Skill description triggers on squash requests but nothing maps the trigger to the squash mode
minor.summary: The frontmatter description still advertises 'prepare a PR squash-merge subject and body' and now adds the 'squash message' and 'squash-merge commit for PR N' triggers, but the forked skill picks the mode only from a token in $ARGUMENTS. When the caller matches a squash trigger and invokes the skill with just the PR number, capture and build run in merge mode and the output is a 'Merge PR #N -- <title>' subject, the opposite of what was asked. No error is shown. README.md:328 was reworded from 'squash-merge subject' to 'merge subject' for this reason, but the description was not.
fix: Reword the description so a squash request carries the token, e.g. '... prepare a PR squash-merge commit (pass squash or --squash after the PR number) ...', and drop 'squash-merge subject and body' from the default-mode sentence.
Add one line to the Arguments paragraph: when the developer's request names a squash message and no mode token is present, the run uses merge mode; the caller passes `squash` after the PR number.

minor.name: An unknown mode token is filed under 'the developer retitles the PR'
minor.summary:
SKILL.md:74-77 lists 'an unknown mode token' among the build problems that 'editing the text cannot fix ... and the developer retitles the PR'. Retitling never fixes a bad mode token. The skill's own argument rule (SKILL.md:16-19) already turns all three forms into `--squash` and stops on anything else, so build cannot see an unknown token on the skill's route. The parenthetical sends the agent to the wrong fix.

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md Step 2 lists 'an unknown mode token' among the stop-class build problems, then closes the sentence with 'editing the text cannot fix it, and the developer retitles the PR'. Retitling never fixes an unknown mode token (merge_commit_msg.py squash_mode, lines 427-431, refuses it before any gh call); the token comes from the arguments, which the skill already validates in its Arguments paragraph (lines 18-19) and always normalizes to --squash. The remedy text contradicts the cause it is attached to.

Also (overall): SKILL.md Step 2 lists 'an unknown mode token' with the PR-state, title, gh and config refusals and then says 'editing the text cannot fix it, and the developer retitles the PR'. Retitling never fixes an unknown mode token: squash_mode() in merge_commit_msg.py:427-431 refuses it based on the arguments alone. The Arguments paragraph (SKILL.md:18-19) already stops the run on an extra token before any command runs, so the entry also contradicts that earlier stop.
fix: Drop 'an unknown mode token' from the build list at SKILL.md:76, or move it to its own clause: 'an unknown mode token: report it and stop (the argument split above passes only `--squash`)'.
Move 'an unknown mode token' out of the retitle sentence into its own clause, e.g. 'An unknown mode token is an argument error: report it and stop.'
Drop 'an unknown mode token' from the list, since the skill passes only --squash and its own argument check (lines 18-19) already stops on any other token.
Remove ', an unknown mode token' from SKILL.md:76, or reword the sentence end to 'report it and stop; editing the text cannot fix it (the developer retitles the PR or reruns with a valid mode)'.

minor.name: Common Mistakes mode-mismatch row overstates what build refuses
minor.summary: The new row 'Running build in a different mode than capture | Pass --squash to both, or to neither' frames any mismatch as a mistake, but run_build (merge_commit_msg.py lines 387-389) auto-selects squash mode when line 1 is the squash subject, so a squash skeleton built without --squash succeeds and writes a squash TXT; only the merge subject under --squash is refused. The same SKILL.md (lines 89-90, 'A rebuild needs no flag') and README line 282-283 state the auto-detection, so the table rule is contradicted by the skill's own text.
fix: Reword the row to the one refused direction: 'Passing --squash to build for a merge-mode skeleton | Run capture with --squash too, or drop the flag from build.'
Keep the row and add 'build without the flag takes the mode from line 1' to its Fix cell.

minor.name: Docs promise a Conventional-Commit title check; the code checks only the Word(scope): shape
minor.summary: SKILL.md:38-39, message_format.md:50-51 and README.md (capture bullet) say a squash-mode PR title must be a Conventional-Commit subject. title_problem (merge_commit_msg.py:136-140) only calls subject_parts, whose regex `^([A-Za-z]+)(?:\(([^)]*)\))?:\s*(.*)$` (commit_txt.py:40) takes any alphabetic word before the colon. So `WIP: x`, `Note: x`, lowercase `fix: x` and `Plan(x): y` all pass, though reference/commit_format.md:28-40 limits types to Feature/Fix/Refactor/Test/Build/Docs/Chore and says `Plan` is NOT a valid type. The squash subject is the one commit that lands on main, so the docs claim a guarantee the check does not give. D1 chose subject_parts as the parser, so this is a mismatch between the docs and the code, not a code bug.
fix: Reword the three doc spots to describe the shape the code checks, e.g. 'a `Type(scope): summary` subject (any word before the colon)', so they stop implying the commit_format.md type list.
Or tighten title_problem to also match commit_txt's `_HEADER_RULE` (the commit_format.md types), exposed as a public name, and add a squash test for a `WIP:` title.

minor.name: Alias identity test pins an internal name with no outside caller
minor.summary: test_private_name_is_the_same_function asserts commit_txt._subject_parts is subject_parts. The alias's only callers are the module's own two call sites (commit_txt.py:162,208), and nothing outside the module uses it. Renaming those calls to the public name and dropping the alias would change no behavior, yet this test would fail.
fix: Rename the two in-module calls to subject_parts, then remove the _subject_parts alias and this test.
Keep the alias but drop the identity test, since the behavioral CASES test already covers the parser.

minor.name: Squash capture's build --squash instruction is unpinned

GOLDEN pins only the merge-mode wording.
fix: In test_squash_capture_states_the_mode, assert "pass the message to `build --squash` on stdin" in captured.out.

minor.name: Empty-summary branch of the squash title check is untested
minor.summary: title_problem refuses a squash title when kind is None or not summary (merge_commit_msg.py:137-140). The tests only cover kind None (LEGACY_TITLE).
